transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I just keep getting up when I'm really supposed to stay put. 

It's happening a lot lately. I'll be right in the middle of client interviews for my investigator work, or during tutoring sessions... even just at my book club. I just stand up and move around. People are definitely starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
When you are in these situations where you feel the need to move, do you feel an overwhelming sense of worry or anxiety about things that might go wrong in your life?

No, not really. I don't feel worried or anxious about things going wrong. It's not like I'm sitting there stressing over a case or my personal life. I just... I just feel this physical urge to stand up. It's more about my body needing to move than my mind worrying about anything.
When you are in these situations, do you find that you are actually having trouble focusing on the task at hand, or is it mostly just the physical urge to move?

I haven't really noticed any trouble focusing, to be honest. I mean, I'm listening to my clients and I know exactly what's going on in the conversation. It really is just... mostly that physical urge to move. My mind is on the task, but my body just doesn't want to stay in the chair.
When you stand up and move around, does that physical urge to move go away, at least temporarily?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't exactly paid attention to whether the urge actually goes away. I just know that when I stand up, it... it feels a bit better in the moment, like I'm just doing what my body is telling me to do. But I can't say for sure if the feeling completely stops or not.
When you feel that urge to stand up, do you notice any strange or uncomfortable sensations in your legs, such as a crawling, tingling, or aching feeling?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My legs don't tingle or ache or feel like something is crawling on them. It's really just... I just feel like I need to get up and move. There's no weird pain or sensation in my legs at all.
Do you often find that you make careless mistakes in your work or have trouble sustaining your attention during tasks that aren't particularly interesting to you?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my job involves a lot of detail—going through records, watching people, piecing things together—so I have to be pretty careful. I haven't really noticed making careless mistakes, and I can usually stick with a task even if it's a bit tedious. It's just the sitting still part that gets to me.
Does this urge to stand up and move happen more frequently in the evening or when you are trying to relax or go to sleep?

No, I wouldn't say it's worse in the evening or when I'm trying to sleep. It just happens whenever I've been sitting for too long, whether it's the middle of the day or at night. It's not really tied to a time of day, just to being stuck in one place.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you struggle with this same need to get up and move around while in the classroom?

Yes, I did. My grade-school report cards actually always said that I was bright, but I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. It's funny, my mother still jokes about it now. She says I treated every classroom like a crime scene that I had to pace through. So, yes, that need to get up and move around has definitely been there since I was young.
